newsitem.title: FRANCE: Group wants CFF 1995 accounts overturned.
newsitem.headline: Group wants CFF 1995 accounts overturned.

text.p: A shareholders' action group has filed legal action to overturn approval of the 1995 accounts of distressed property lender Credit Foncier de France (CFF), business daily La Tribune reported on Tuesday.
The request was filed in commercial court by the shareholders' rights group ADAM which has argued that the 13.6 billion francs worth of property provisions in the 1995 accounts were too high.

Credit Foncier, due to be taken over by state-owned bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC) and wound down, posted a 10.8 billion franc loss for 1995. It swung back to a 402 million franc profit for the first half of 1996.

The 1995 accounts were approved by 52.65 percent amid heated debate at CFF's annual meeting on June 28. ADAM is claiming that the vote should be annulled because of irregularities involving millions of votes, the newspaper said.
The commercial court is to rule on Thursday on the request by ADAM which has been contesting the state-organised takeover, the newspaper said.
The daily said a decision by the commercial court in the group's favour would force a higher offer to shareholders for their shares.

"A decision by the court in favour of ADAM would not jeopardise the takeover of CFF by the Caisse des depots but would result in a revision in the price fixed by the state (of 70 francs)," said La Tribune.
ADAM, which says Credit Foncier shares are worth at least 100 francs, is seeking an independent evaluation of the property lender's worth.
Also Tuesday is the deadline for the Conseil des Bourses de Valeur (CBV) stockmarket regulator to rule on the receivability of CDC's bid.
